**Visual analysis:**

- The image shows **three wheat spikes** side by side against a bare soil background.
- **Left spike**: Healthy green — compact, fully green glumes and florets.
- **Middle spike**: Completely **bleached/whitened** — straw-colored glumes throughout the entire head.
- **Right spike**: Also heavily **bleached/tan-colored**, similar to the middle.

**Key diagnostic features:**
- The contrast between the healthy green spike (left) and the bleached spikes (middle, right) is the central feature.
- The bleaching is diffuse and affects entire spikelets/the whole head, not just localized lesions.
- No dark powdery masses (ruling out Loose Smut, Dwarf Bunt).
- No orange/red pustules (ruling out Stem Rust or Stripe Rust).
- No leaf lesions visible — the disease is centered on the head.
- This "premature bleaching" of the entire spike is the hallmark symptom of **Fusarium Head Blight (Head Scab)** — the causal pathogen (Fusarium spp.) causes rapid whitening/bleaching of spikelets, spreading to encompass the whole spike in severe cases.

**Eliminated alternatives:**
- Loose Smut / Dwarf Bunt → would show dark sooty masses replacing grain
- Stripe Rust / Stem Rust → pustules on leaves/stems, not spike bleaching
- Barley Yellow Dwarf → yellowing of leaves, not head bleaching
- Septoria / Tan Spot → leaf blotches, not head symptoms
